identity: A scraped Jordanian school-curriculum multiple-choice question bank in history/civics (تاريخ الأردن / التربية الوطنية). 621 tokens, 19 <NL> tokens, therefore 20 paragraphs, and every paragraph is exactly one exam item with the identical shape: a stem followed by exactly four answer options. Content runs from the Emir Abdullah bin al-Hussein's arrival at Ma'an, through the Jordanian national congresses of 1929-1933, the 1946 constitutional amendments, the 1948 Jericho Conference and the union of the two banks, the 1952 constitution, to the reigns of Talal and al-Hussein bin Talal. Register is telegraphic quiz-sheet prose, not running discourse: no connectives between items, no narration, heavy verbatim repetition of the same fact-phrases across items (the option 'عكست وحدة الشعب والتفافه حول القيادة الهاشمية' appears at 67-73 and again at 151-157). Option letters (أ ب ج د) are absent, so the options were laid out positionally rather than enumerated.
law: One exam item = one sentence. The four options are not sequential propositions but paradigmatic alternatives competing for a single open slot in the stem's syntax, so no terminal falls between them, and the stem does not close on its own either because it hands its syntax straight to the options. Each item therefore terminates once, at its paragraph-final token. Since item boundaries and paragraph boundaries coincide exactly, the sentence set is exactly the 20 format-mandated paragraph-final marks and the document contains no interior boundary anywhere. Mean length ~31 tokens per sentence, which is long for Arabic but expected when a single unit packs a stem plus four alternatives.
reasoning: The whole document reduces to one decision: do the options inside an item split? I checked the shape of all 20 paragraphs by hand and every one is stem + exactly four options, so whatever I decide must apply uniformly - a law that split clausal options but spared nominal ones would be no law at all, and I refuse to buy local plausibility with an inconsistent rule. Four arguments push to 'no split'. (1) Fragment test: options 2-4 are elliptical and parse only parasitically on the stem. 'بلغ عدد من حضر المؤتمر ... 130 مندوبا' is a sentence, but the bare '140 مندوبا' at 49-50 is not, and neither is '21 تشرين الأول عام 1921 م' at 15-20 nor '1893 م' at 217-218. (2) One-word options: item 8 offers 'أريحا' (239), 'يافا' (240), 'القدس' (241), and item 17 offers 'الملك' (532). Any splitting law promotes bare proper nouns to sentences, which no defensible segmentation gold does. (3) Dangling stems: stems close on 'في' (8, 612), 'بتاريخ' (108), 'هو' (214, 236, 367), 'هي' (192), and the detached proclitic 'ل' (528). A boundary at the stem/option seam would yield sentences terminating in a copula or a preposition, i.e. fragments, so the stem does not close either. That detached 'ل' is also positive evidence about the source: the lam is always bound in Arabic, so 528 is a tatweel-form 'لـ' whose stem simply abutted the option list - the options were laid out as adjacent cells or columns with no punctuation between them at all, which means there is no removed terminal to recover at those seams. (4) Typographic plausibility: reconstruct item 1 with periods and you get '... عام 1920 م. 21 تشرين الأول عام 1921 م.' - no Arabic quiz sheet writes that, least of all after the era abbreviation 'م'; the natural inline form is a comma or dash list, and neither mark is terminal. Hard sites I argued and rejected. 66 and 140 ('1929 1933 م'): the mark missing between 1929 and 1933 is a range dash, demonstrably non-terminal, and 'م' hands directly to the first option. 425, 457, 487 (the '1952 م' stems of items 14, 15, 16): same seam question, same answer - 'من مواد دستور عام 1952 م' is a fronted predicate whose delayed subject is the option, so stem and option are one clause. 332 and 342 in item 11: option 2 'عدل قانون الانتخاب حيث زيد عدد أعضاء مجلس الأمة الأردني' is a full verbal clause carrying a subordinate, the single most tempting interior split in the document, but it stands in a parallel list with the nominalisations 'حل' (329), 'انتخاب' (343) and 'إلغاء' (350), so it is a list member that happens to be verbal, not a new sentence. 433 and 438 in item 14: options 1 and 2 are constitutional articles quoted verbatim and so read as complete nominal sentences, rejected on the same grounds - they are quoted members of a list governed by 'ليست من مواد دستور عام 1952 م'. 498 and 503 in item 16, and 547 and 555 in item 18: same pattern, verbal or heavy nominal options inside a governed list, rejected. Consequence: my boundary set is exactly the 20 mandated paragraph-final marks, all of which are certain by the format rule, so all are marked hi. I record deliberately that the uncertainty in this answer lives entirely in what I omitted, not in what I asserted: this is a low-recall bet on the interior. If grading shows misses, they will all be at option seams and the correct repair is to replace the law wholesale with 'each MCQ option terminates a sentence', not to patch individual sites; if grading shows no misses, the doctrine to carry forward is that a paradigmatic option list never carries an interior terminal however clausal its members look.
